Adjudicating whether observed global correlations in multi-level physical systems represent genuine causal laws or emergent statistical artifacts is a fundamental challenge across engineering and applied sciences. Such correlations underpin scaling laws, kinetic models, and materials design rules, yet this ambiguity compromises reliable prediction and design. This work introduces the Causal Verification Framework (CVF), a novel analytical methodology that resolves this ambiguity by testing observed correlations against known, low-level physical laws. The CVF inverts standard causal inference from identification to verification. Formalized as a Hierarchical Functional Causal Model (HFCM), the CVF employs targeted analytical intervention tests of stability (invariance under compositional change) and autonomy (invariance under parametric perturbation) to diagnose statistical phantoms — correlations that are contingent, non-autonomous artifacts of aggregation. The framework delivers a causal resolution to the long-standing Enthalpy-Entropy Compensation (EEC) debate, demonstrating the global correlation to be such a phantom. A protein denaturation case study illustrates the CVF's diagnostic power. The CVF provides a principled methodology for causal verification with applications across catalyst screening, process optimization, and materials discovery.
